GTA 6 Locked at 30 FPS: Not Even PS5 Pro Can Handle 60 FPS
78 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Now that GTA 6 is here , and pretty much the whole planet is playing it, the time has come to look at the game and figure out what Rockstar should have done better. One of the most debated topics is the 30 FPS cap, which for many people is unacceptable for a 2026 release, especially considering the hardware capabilities of new-gen consoles.
Not being able to run at 60 FPS is a limitation that has generated intense criticism online, with some people claiming they wouldn’t even buy the game unless Rockstar removes the 30 FPS limit. While I do have my doubts that those who love GTA will manage to stay away from the game just because it’s limited to 30 FPS, the criticism has made the headlines on multiple occasions, without Rockstar directly addressing it.
The time has come for the company to defend its decision for this highly criticized cap.
Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said in an interview that the 30 fps limit comes and not even offering a balanced mode that would increase the setting to 40 fps was a decision whose objective was to allow the game to handle the high complexity of every little thing that moves around you.
Chambers explained that the level of detail included in GTA 6 is so high and complex that finding the right settings doesn’t just come down to a toggle in your game menu. “The frame rate we’ve chosen gives us the right balance of presentation, simulation, and gameplay,” the Rockstar official explained.
With 30 fps enforced on all consoles, including the PS5 Pro, which at first glance would be able to handle 60 fps, is not supposed to offer the downgrade that many people might anticipate when checking out these specifications on paper. This is because it is entirely custom-built, meaning that Rockstar has found a way to deliver the smooth experience you’d expect without compromising what you see on your TV.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The more important part is that not even the PS5 Pro would have been able to handle 60 fps in GTA 6, and the reason is the same high complexity of everything around you in the game. Leonida is a vast world - the largest open world ever in a game - so the amount of information a console has to handle is enormous.
I play the game on my regular, non-Pro PlayStation 5, and I have to say that the 30 fps limit makes the gameplay feel as smooth and fluid as possible. I’m certain that a higher setting would have altered the gameplay, and after I tried playing it on a PS5 Pro, this thing became more obvious.
Sure, the upgrade from a regular PS5 to a Pro is easily noticeable, and I do admit that this is probably the best console to play GTA 6 today. I’m also seeing people complaining about the Xbox Series S, where the fps drop is more common, but everything seems to be running properly on the Series X.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution But at the end of the day, the PS5 indeed has upgraded internals, but Rockstar says it has preferred to use the graphics processors and upscaling technology specifically to “increase the game’s visual fidelity.”
Chambers said in a separate interview that GTA 6 is not like every other game that went live so far, so while on paper it might look like a latest-gen console like the PS5 Pro would be able to handle everything you throw at it, the new Grand Theft Auto is different.
“The complexity of simulating and rendering the environments and inhabitants in a world the scale of Leonida, while maintaining the density, visual fidelity, and player agency we envisaged, places extraordinary demands on the hardware,” he was quoted as saying.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The conclusion is simple, in his opinion: PS5 is not powerful enough to run the game at higher frame rates.
Without a doubt, it’ll be interesting to see how Rockstar handles all this high complexity once GTA 6 lands on PC. There’s still no ETA as to when this is projected to happen, but given the fast hardware ecosystem, capping the FPS limit wouldn’t make as much sense in the PC world. Unless Rockstar wants to make the game playable on as many configurations as possible, that is.
Previous reports on the matter suggested that the PC version of GTA 6 could go live as soon as 2027, with some sources claiming that Rockstar plans to keep it exclusive to new-gen consoles for at least one year.
Others said the spring of 2027 is a more realistic expectation for a PC version of GTA 6, especially as Rockstar wants to capitalize on this amazing interest the world is showing for the game. Unsurprisingly, the company has so far remained tight-lipped on a PC version of GTA 6, so nothing is set in stone at this point, including the FPS cap.
